subject: Re: Performance SLO + VPC qualification — ACME / Redwood Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC qualification - ACME call notes

Jordan — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Short recap + action items from our side so we can qualify Redwood Private for ACME's performance SLOs.

Key performance asks you mentioned:
- p95 end-to-end latency goal: <= 200 ms for streaming responses (token-level streaming to the browser).
- Sustained throughput: ~600 requests/minute with average request sizes ~250 tokens and bursts to 1,500 rpm.
- Concurrency: ~80 concurrent streaming sessions during peak.
- Streaming behavior: server-sent events (chunked HTTP/gRPC streaming), keep-alive connections preferred to avoid TLS handshake overhead.

Private/VPC items we need to qualify:
1) Network path: peering vs VPN. You mentioned AWS VPC peering as preferred; please confirm VPC IDs and whether cross-account peering is possible.
2) Expected RTT between ACME app tier and Redwood Private nodes (target <= 25 ms one-way for comfortable p95 budget).
3) Egress/NAT: do you have stable egress IPs or NAT gateways we can whitelist? If not, will you allow routing via a customer-managed NAT?
4) Firewalls / ports: which outbound ports are allowed for long-lived TLS (443) and whether you allow persistent websockets/grpc over TLS.
5) MTU and any intermediate proxies/load balancers (AWS ALB/NLB) that terminate TLS or do TCP passthrough.
6) Any corporate proxies or IDS that could buffer/inspect streaming payloads.
7) Test window: propose a 30-45 minute network validation window where we can run traceroutes, TCP handshake/latency tests, and a lightweight token-stream test.

Deliverables / next steps from ACME to Redwood:
- VPC diagram (peering/VPN details), route tables, and NAT/gateway IPs.
- Contact for network ops (we'll need an on-call during testing).

Redwood deliverables:
- A checklist of required ports and IPs to whitelist, and a short-runbook for the test.
- Proposed schedule for the network validation (I can do tomorrow morning PT or Monday).
- A pre-configured lightweight streaming test that uses an ACME-provided endpoint and returns perf metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, bytes/sec, concurrency behavior).

Attaching: request for a VPC diagram and a template traceroute output (we'll provide our sample command to run).

Thanks — I looped in Aditya (networking lead) and Laura (solutions) to help run the tests and capture topology requirements.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
https://redwoodinference.com
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC qualification - ACME call notes

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Attaching the VPC diagram and a recent traceroute to one of our app nodes. Answers inline below.

Quick answers:
- Peering: We prefer AWS VPC peering (cross-account). VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e. We can set up the peering connection and route table entries if you provide the Redwood VPC CIDR and expected subnets.
- RTT: Internal measurements show ~12-18 ms one-way between our app ELB and the target RDW subnet in us-west-2 — that should be within your target.
- Egress: We have NAT gateways with stable egress IPs: 54.201.11.45 and 54.201.11.46 — you can whitelist those.
- Ports: 443 (TLS) is allowed outbound. We use ALBs in front of the app that terminate TLS; we can also configure TCP passthrough if needed.
- Proxies: No corporate HTTP proxy in the path for traffic between VPCs.

Attachments: acme-vpc-diagram.pdf, traceroute-20260404.txt

We can do the network window tomorrow (Sunday) at 09:00 PT; IT Ops is available and I can be on the call.

—
Jordan Miller
Director, Platform Engineering | ACME Corp
jordan.miller@acmecorp.com | +1 (206) 555-9876
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC qualification - ACME call notes

Jordan — perfect, that answers a lot. Quick clarifications before the test tomorrow at 09:00 PT:

1) Streaming semantics: we'll run a streaming token test over chunked HTTP (keep-alive TLS). Can you confirm the ALB is configured for HTTP/1.1 keep-alive or that TCP passthrough will be available? If ALB terminates TLS and buffers responses, streaming semantics may be affected.

2) NAT egress: thanks for the two IPs — we'll provide those to our security team to ensure inbound management callbacks (if any) are allowed for test instrumentation.

3) Can you run and share a small set of network checks before our window:
   - traceroute to the target Redwood test IP (we'll provide)
   - curl -w "%{time_starttransfer}" against a dummy endpoint to capture TTFB
   - a simple TCP ping (hping3 or tcping) to measure handshake time

4) For throughput/concurrency validation we'll perform a controlled load with 100 concurrent streaming clients for 15 minutes and capture p50/p95 token latencies. Is there a maintenance window you prefer? 09:00 PT tomorrow works for us too.

I'll put together the runbook and short script for the tests and share a Drive link in a few minutes. Aditya will lead the test from Redwood and will need an on-call from IT Ops for packet capture/troubleshooting if needed.

Thanks — see you tomorrow.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC qualification - ACME call notes

All set for 09:00 PT. Confirming:
- ALB will be left in TCP passthrough mode for the test window (no TLS termination at the ALB).
- NAT egress IPs above are in our firewall allowlist for the session.
- On-call for network ops: IT Ops alias (it-ops@acmecorp.com) and Samir Patel (samir.patel@acmecorp.com) will be on the bridge.

Attached: small packet capture from the traceroute run and a TCP handshake log (traceroute-20260404.txt).

If the test looks good we'll schedule a second, longer throughput run with 2-4 hours notice to validate sustained concurrency.

—
Jordan Miller
